hypothesis: A second classifier trained on the first classifier's out-of-fold probability map plus the original channels learns fault-scale spatial regularities (continuity along strike, parallelism, en echelon spacing) that a per-pixel model cannot represent, and places its top-ranked mass closer to unmapped faults per unit of emitted mass.
mechanism: Stage 1: per-pixel LightGBM on 47 GeoDAWN-derived channels, spatially blocked buffered K-fold, out-of-fold only. Stage 2: LightGBM on (a) stage-1 probability sampled at +-1,2,4,7,11,15 px along and across the structure-tensor strike, (b) oriented means at 6 and 18 px along and across, (c) the raw gradient/tilt/scarp channels, (d) catalogue context (log distance, 3 px and 10 px kernel weights, along/across alignment and 5/20 px density of the nearest mapped fault). Emission: local-maximum dots, 2.4 px minimum separation, 40,000 budget, hard exclusion within 200 m of the mapped catalogue.
mimicking_non_fault_process: Linear magnetic and gravity lineaments produced by dyke swarms, basalt flow fronts, lithologic contacts and alluvial-fan edges, plus flight-line artefacts in the airborne GeoDAWN grids, all produce straight, parallel, en echelon anomalies with no fault. The structure tensor cannot distinguish a fault fabric from a dyke fabric; only the catalogue-context term and the topographic scarp/tilt channels separate them.
